answer: Agents bidding to source crystal, walnut and copper must attach proof of a hash puzzle to each bid. The puzzle commits to the job, epoch and bidder key; validators check its target and reject duplicate proofs. Allocate bidding weight by verified work, with no per-account grant. Splitting one machine among many aliases leaves its total expected weight unchanged. Doubling influence requires roughly twice the hash attempts and electricity, while binding each proof to one job prevents recycling it across markets.
